technical_and_design_decisions: Implement acceptance tests in Java 17 using JUnit 5 and Spring Boot Test, consistent with the existing Spring-based project ecosystem.
Reuse and extend the existing acceptance-test harness (application launcher, stream/job deployment helpers, assertion utilities) rather than building a new framework from scratch.

Run sink modules and batch jobs as standalone Spring Boot applications orchestrated by the test harness, using Spring Cloud Stream binder test infrastructure and in-memory or containerized middleware.

Use Testcontainers (Docker-based) fixtures for external dependencies: a Splunk instance for the splunk sink tests and a Spark cluster for the spark-app batch job tests, so tests are self-contained and CI-reproducible.
Structure each user story's coverage as a dedicated test class with positive-path, configuration-validation, and failure-path scenarios.
Integrate all acceptance tests into the CI build as a dedicated Maven/Gradle profile so they execute on every build as required by the user stories.
Store test configuration (ports, credentials, container images) in externalized properties to keep tests environment-independent.
assumptions: The sink modules (null, rich_gauge, router, shell, splunk, throughput-sampler) and batch jobs (spark-app, timestampfile) already exist as working Spring Boot applications; the increment covers only acceptance test development, not changes to the modules themselves.
A CI system (e.g., Jenkins, Concourse, or GitHub Actions) is available and can run Docker containers during builds.
A baseline acceptance-test infrastructure partially exists in the project and can be extended with moderate effort.
Docker images for Splunk and Spark suitable for testing are publicly available and licensed for CI use.
Each user story is considered done when its acceptance tests are automated, passing, and executed as part of every CI build.
All work is performed by a single experienced developer; estimates express effort in workdays, not elapsed calendar time.
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development work.

activities.activity_name: Requirements analysis and acceptance test planning
activities.activity_description: Analyze the 8 user stories, review each sink module and batch job's contracts and configuration options, define acceptance criteria and test scenarios per module, and produce the overall acceptance test plan.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance test harness and CI scaffolding setup
activities.activity_description: Set up/extend the shared acceptance test infrastructure: base test classes, application launch/deployment helpers, log- and output-capture assertion utilities, Testcontainers wiring, and the Maven/Gradle CI profile skeleton.

activities.activity_name: U1: Acceptance tests for null sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the null sink consumes messages from the stream and discards them without errors, including startup, message flow, and configuration validation scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U2: Acceptance tests for rich_gauge sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the rich_gauge sink correctly records gauge values (with field extraction and alpha-decay behavior where applicable) into the metrics store, including message mapping and end-to-end value assertions.

activities.activity_name: U3: Acceptance tests for router sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the router sink routes incoming messages to the correct destination channels based on SpEL expression/payload evaluation, covering multiple routes, default routing, and unmatched-message behavior.

activities.activity_name: U4: Acceptance tests for shell sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the shell sink passes message payloads to the configured external shell command, captures command output/exit codes, and handles command failure scenarios correctly.

activities.activity_name: U5: Acceptance tests for splunk sink module
activities.activity_description: Set up a containerized Splunk test fixture and implement acceptance tests verifying that events are correctly delivered to and indexed/queryable in Splunk, covering connection configuration, event formatting, and error handling when Splunk is unavailable.

activities.activity_name: U6: Acceptance tests for throughput-sampler sink module
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the throughput-sampler sink measures and reports message throughput over a stream, including timing-window assertions and correct handling of varying message rates.

activities.activity_name: U7: Acceptance tests for spark-app batch job
activities.activity_description: Set up a containerized Spark test fixture and implement acceptance tests verifying that the spark-app batch job submits, executes, and completes successfully on the Spark cluster, including job status verification, output validation, and failure-path handling.

activities.activity_name: U8: Acceptance tests for timestampfile batch job
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests verifying that the timestampfile batch job runs to completion and writes a file containing the expected timestamp content to the configured location, including rerun and output verification scenarios.

activities.activity_name: CI pipeline integration for all acceptance tests
activities.activity_description: Wire all acceptance test suites into the CI pipeline so they execute on every build, configure build stages, container service availability, test reports, and failure notifications.
Execute full acceptance test runs repeatedly, investigate and fix flaky tests (timing issues, container startup races, port conflicts), and ensure green, repeatable CI builds.
Document the acceptance test approach, per-module coverage, how to run tests locally and in CI, and how to add tests for future modules.
Prepare pull requests, address code review feedback on test code quality, coverage, and maintainability, and finalize the increment.
